lines.label: Voting rights: black
lines.working: Black voting rights 46.4% ÷ 25% × 4 = 7.43, capped at 4. Each shareholder counts by the value of their shares.

lines.label: Voting rights: black women
lines.working: Black women's voting rights 22.1% ÷ 10% × 2 = 4.41, capped at 2.

lines.label: Economic interest: black
lines.working: Black economic interest 46.4% ÷ 25% × 4 = 7.43, capped at 4. That is 16.1% held by black shareholders without acquisition debt + 30.3% net value of the indebted black shareholders' stakes (their share of the R290 000 000 company value less their debt).

lines.label: Economic interest: black women
lines.working: Black women's economic interest 14.3% ÷ 10% × 2 = 2.85, capped at 2. That is 6.9% held by black women without acquisition debt + 7.4% net value of the indebted black shareholders' stakes (their share of the R290 000 000 company value less their debt).

lines.label: Economic interest: designated groups
lines.working: Designated groups' economic interest 3.5% ÷ 3% × 3 = 3.50, capped at 3.
lines.toolkitNote: Toolkit formula fault (its target is cut to "0.0"): its own measure 3.50% against the real 3% target gives 3.00; the toolkit shows 0.00.

lines.label: Economic interest: new entrants
lines.working: Black new entrants' economic interest 31.3% ÷ 2% × 2 = 31.26, capped at 2.
lines.toolkitNote: Toolkit formula fault (its target is cut to "0.0"): its own measure 31.26% against the real 2% target gives 2.00; the toolkit shows 0.00.

lines.label: Net value
lines.working: Black economic interest after acquisition debt 46.4% ÷ 100% × 8 = 3.72. Sub-minimum 3.2 points: met.
lines.toolkitNote: Toolkit formula fault: it nets an indebted shareholder's stake by a formula that depends on the row the shareholder sits in, and counts the whole stake as black. Its own figures, netted the one way and for the black share only, give 46.45% black economic interest → 3.72; the toolkit shows 2.47.

lines.label: Learning programmes
lines.working: Each black group is measured against its effective-EAP share of 3.5% × R68.49m leviable and can earn up to its share of 6 points. African male R190,303 ÷ R1.09m → 0.48 of 2.72; African female R112,279 ÷ R1.08m → 0.28 of 2.70. Bursaries are scored on their own line. F & G course costs are capped at 25.0% and other costs at 15.0% of all training spend (R375,538), per group share.

lines.label: Bursaries
lines.working: Category A rows marked as higher-education bursaries for black students, each group against its EAP share of 2.5% × R68.49m: none recorded. A stipend counts only for a learner who was unemployed or on a fixed-term contract.

lines.label: Disabled learners
lines.working: Black learners with disabilities: R0 recognised ÷ R205,478 (0.3% × R68.49m) × 4 = 0.00 (max 4).

lines.label: Learnerships / apprenticeships / internships
lines.working: Black learners in categories B, C and D (employed or not), each group against its EAP share of 5% × 68 headcount: African male 3 ÷ 1.54 → 2.72 of 2.72; African female 1 ÷ 1.53 → 1.76 of 2.70.

lines.label: Absorption (bonus)
lines.working: 0 unemployed or fixed-term black learner(s) completed a learnership, apprenticeship or internship and were absorbed: 0 ÷ 68 headcount = 0.0% vs 5% target → 0.00 (max 5).

lines.label: Graduation bonus
lines.working: At least one ESD beneficiary graduated from Enterprise to Supplier Development: 1 of 1.

lines.label: Jobs created bonus
lines.working: At least one job was created through ESD initiatives: 1 of 1.

achieved.note: The toolkit shows Level 5; its level lookup drops a level exactly on a threshold, or uses the uncorrected ownership lines.

discounted.note: The toolkit shows Level 6; its Skills sub-minimum test reads empty cells and always fails.
